column1: # PRESET DORMANT-VALUE FRONTIER — armed values that are not consumed on the
# route their preset currently takes, and the neighbouring key that wakes them.
# Columns:  yaml-file <TAB> dotted-key <TAB> value <TAB> state <TAB> count <TAB> class <TAB> note
# `state` is part of the IDENTITY, not a payload. That is the whole design: when
# a gate key flips, the row's identity changes, the exact-set diff reports both
# a new `live` row and a stale `dormant` one, and somebody has to look at the
#   dormant        carried but not consumed on this preset's route.
#   dormant-woken  the gate is set to its waking value, so the number is live.
#                  The note MUST carry the measurement, because this is the
#                  state in which an unexercised value governs a real run.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `bab.batch_size: 64` sat unconsumed until `reorder_bab`
# flipped, and then produced an 11.7x memory regression — 6.3 GB to 73.4 GB —
# on a unified-memory host where an over-admission is a global OOM rather than a
# refusal. Nothing about the value had ever been measured, because it had never
# applied to anything. It is neither a dead value (64 is a fine batch size) nor
# a runtime clear (nothing overwrote it): it is a live value on a route nobody
# was taking, which is why the other two yaml-side checks are both blind to it.
# Pairs are declared in `DORMANT_UNTIL` in preset_arrival_ratchet.rs; this file
# holds their per-yaml state. An empty body means no pair is currently tracked.
